source.title: On Some Open Problems on Maximal Curves

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an F_{q^2}-maximal curve X over the finite field F_{q^2} whose Frobenius linear series D = |(q+1)P_0| has projective dimension 3 and whose generic D-order sequence has third entry ε_2 = 3, equivalently whose D-order sequence is (0, 1, 3, q)?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of a Frobenius-dimension-3 maximal curve with ε_2 = 3.

evidence.quote: In [2] it was asked whether the following three cases actually occur for maximal curves with Frobenius dimension 3: (A) ǫ2 = 3;
Therefore, the answer to question (A) in Introduction is obtained. Theorem 3.5. There exists a maximal curves over F272 with Frobenius dimension 3 and with D-order sequence (0, 1, 3, 27).

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an F_{q^2}-maximal curve X over F_{q^2} whose Frobenius linear series has projective dimension 3, whose generic D-order sequence satisfies ε_2 = 2, and for which there is an F_{q^2}-rational point P such that the second (D, P)-order is j_2(P) = 3?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of a Frobenius-dimension-3 maximal curve with ε_2 = 2 and j_2(P) = 3.

evidence.quote: (B) ǫ2 = 2, j2(P) = 3 for some Fq2-rational point P;

We are going to prove the following result, which provides an affirmative answer to both questions (B) and (C) in Introduction. Theorem 4.1. Let F = K(z, t) be the function field defined over K = F49 by the equation z16 = t(t + 1)6. Then the Frobenius dimension of F is 3, the D-order sequence of F is (0, 1, 2, 7), and there exists an F49-rational place P of F such that j2(P) = 3 = 8− ⌊ 2/3 (8)⌋.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an F_{q^2}-maximal curve X over F_{q^2} whose Frobenius linear series has projective dimension 3, whose generic D-order sequence satisfies ε_2 = 2, and for which there is an F_{q^2}-rational point P such that the second (D, P)-order is j_2(P) = q + 1 - floor((2/3)(q + 1))?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of a Frobenius-dimension-3 maximal curve with ε_2 = 2 and the large exceptional value of j_2(P).

evidence.quote: (C) ǫ2 = 2, j2(P) = q + 1 − [2/3 (q + 1)] for some Fq2-rational point P.

We are going to prove the following result, which provides an affirmative answer to both questions (B) and (C) in Introduction. Theorem 4.1. Let F = K(z, t) be the function field defined over K = F49 by the equation z16 = t(t + 1)6. Then the Frobenius dimension of F is 3, the D-order sequence of F is (0, 1, 2, 7), and there exists an F49-rational place P of F such that j2(P) = 3 = 8− ⌊ 2/3 (8)⌋.
